competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Overview
key_points: Agent Framework combines AutoGen's simple agent abstractions with Semantic Kernel's enterprise features
Two primary capabilities: Agents (individual LLM-driven agents with tools/MCP) and Workflows (graph-based multi-step orchestration)
Supports Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Ollama providers
Workflows provide type-safe routing, checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop support
1.0 GA on April 2, 2026 as the successor to both AutoGen and Semantic Kernel

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows Overview
key_points: Workflows are predefined sequences of operations that can include AI agents as components
Five key capabilities: Type Safety, Flexible Control Flow, External Integration (HITL), Checkpointing, Multi-Agent Orchestration
Two complementary APIs: Functional (@workflow decorator, experimental Python) and Graph (WorkflowBuilder)
HITL in Functional API via ctx.request_info() — suspends workflow and waits for external input
HITL in Graph API via RequestPort pattern — emits RequestInfoEvent for external handling
Both APIs support streaming, HITL, checkpoints, and events with identical observable results

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Functional Workflow API
key_points: @workflow decorator converts async functions into FunctionalWorkflow objects with native Python control flow
@step decorator adds result caching, event emission, and per-step checkpointing for expensive operations
WorkflowRunContext (ctx) provides request_info() for HITL, get_state()/set_state() for persistent state, add_event() for custom events
HITL suspension returns WorkflowRunState.IDLE_WITH_PENDING_REQUESTS — resume via .run(responses={request_id: value})
@step-decorated functions return cached results on HITL resume, preventing re-execution
Supports asyncio.gather for fan-out parallelism, agent calls as plain function calls, and .as_agent() wrapping

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework HITL Workflows (Dedicated Page)
key_points: RequestPort is a communication channel that allows executors to send requests and receive responses
Executors in graph-based workflow send requests via ctx.request_info() and handle responses with @response_handler decorator
Agent tool approval via ToolApprovalRequestContent (C#) / function_approval_request (Python) pauses workflow for human approval before sensitive tool execution
Checkpoints save pending HITL requests — on restore, re-emitted as RequestInfoEvent for external handling
Full runnable samples available: python/samples/03-workflows/functional/hitl_review.py

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows - Executors
key_points: Executors are fundamental building blocks — autonomous processing units that receive typed messages and produce outputs
Executors can be custom logic components (APIs, transformations) or AI agents with LLMs
IWorkflowContext provides SendMessageAsync, YieldOutputAsync for graph message routing and output emission
Python supports @handler and @response_handler decorators, @executor function decorator, and multiple handler methods per type
HITL flows through RequestPort — executors send requests, external systems listen for RequestInfoEvent and respond

competitors.title: Microsoft Agent Framework at BUILD 2026: Agent Harness, Hosted Agents, CodeAct
key_points: MAF 1.0 GA on April 2, 2026 — convergence of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel
Agent Harness: production patterns including ToolApprovalAgent for HITL tool approval flows
Foundry Hosted Agents: scale-to-zero, VM-isolated sessions, built-in observability, persistent filesystem
CodeAct: collapses multi-tool loops into single Python program — 52.4% latency reduction, 63.9% token savings
FIDES: Flow Integrity Deterministic Enforcement System — information-flow control for prompt injection prevention
GitHub Copilot SDK integration, Handoff orchestration, Agent Skills for modular capability injection

competitors.title: Stop Prompt Injection from Hijacking Your Agent — FIDES in Agent Framework
key_points: Prompt injection is #1 risk on OWASP LLM Top 10
FIDES provides deterministic information-flow control with integrity (trusted/untrusted) and confidentiality (public/private) labels
Labels propagate automatically through middleware — no hand-rolled allowlists needed
Deterministic enforcement vs heuristic system prompts that fail silently
Available as first-class middleware in Agent Framework
